WEB DEVELOPMENT & MODEL OPTIMIZATION

From scan to web

The team carried out the campus aerial survey and scan reconstruction in RealityScan. My work focused on subsequent web development and model optimization.

A lighter campus model

Prepared a lighter mesh and textures for the web preview and removed small floating scan fragments. Export records report 2.98 million faces before reduction and 1.01 million afterward, excluding the replacement buildings.

Viewer & scene integration

Built the Three.js viewer, integrated the optimized scan with replacement geometry, and implemented camera views and reversible scan/reconstruction comparisons.

01 / LIBRARY

Library reconstruction

Facade & roof

The reconstructed upper building uses regular glazing, white diagonal supports, a rear wall and main roof elements, based on the scan and aerial photographs.

Local replacement

The rebuilt geometry is integrated as a reversible local replacement. Surrounding terrain, terraces and the building base remain from the scan.

Visual reconstruction

Dimensions and details are approximate, based on the available references. This is a visual reconstruction rather than a measured survey or construction model.

02 / GYMNASIUM

Gymnasium reconstruction

Envelope & openings

Main wall planes, recessed glazing, columns and entrance volumes were rebuilt using the scan and aerial photographs as references.

Roof & ground

The rooftop court and enclosure were modeled while retaining scanned roof equipment. Local ground repairs use heights sampled from the scanned site.

Exterior focus

This stage focuses on exterior form and facade structure. Small details and interiors remain simplified; the surrounding campus uses the optimized scan.
